says: When no entry is selected in the policy file list, only Add key and Export are available; Add value, Delete value, Edit and Forget are disabled.
When a key is selected, Add key, Add value, Delete value, Forget and Export are available and Edit is disabled.
When a value is selected, Forget is available; Add key, Add value and Export are disabled; Edit and Delete value are available only if the value is not a deletion marker.
The policy file list is refreshed only when the REG import dialog is confirmed with OK; a cancelled import leaves the list as it was.
Export REG starts from the selected key's path, or from an empty path (the whole file) when nothing is selected, and exports the user file as the user hive when the user policy file is being edited.
When the delete dialog opens, none of its three options is chosen and the value name is empty; the key shown is the key the person selected.

When OK is pressed, choosing 'clear first' or 'purge' is accepted without further input. Choosing 'delete one value' with an empty value name is refused with the message "You must enter a value name." and the dialog stays open. With no option chosen, nothing happens.
When Escape is pressed in the dialog, it closes as cancelled and nothing in it is applied.
The value name box can be typed in only while 'delete one value' is chosen; for the other two options it is disabled.
When Escape is pressed in the dialog, it closes as cancelled and nothing in it is applied.
When the key name dialog is confirmed with OK, the typed name is returned; when it is cancelled, an empty name is returned and no key is added.
When Escape is pressed in the dialog, it closes as cancelled and nothing in it is applied.
A number value can be entered up to 4294967295 for a 32-bit DWord and up to 18446744073709551615 for a 64-bit QWord; the box opens showing the current value.
When Escape is pressed in the dialog, it closes as cancelled and nothing in it is applied.
In hexadecimal mode, any text the person has typed is first read as a hex number, and a non-empty box is then redisplayed as the value in upper-case hex digits without a prefix.
In decimal mode, the standard number box formatting is used.
When typed text is confirmed in hexadecimal mode, it is read as a hex number and the box is redisplayed as the resulting value; in decimal mode the standard number box check applies.

Typed hex text is read as a number. Text beyond the allowed range is replaced by the maximum, text starting with a minus sign that overflows by the minimum. Text that cannot be read as hex leaves the value unchanged; empty text is ignored.
When Escape is pressed in the dialog, it closes as cancelled and nothing in it is applied.
When Escape is pressed in the dialog, it closes as cancelled and nothing in it is applied.
A new value starts with an empty name and the type 'String' preselected.

When the new-value dialog is confirmed with OK, the value is created with the chosen type: String, Expandable string, List of strings, 32-bit DWord or 64-bit QWord, under the typed name. A cancelled dialog yields no type or name. The dialog itself does not refuse an empty name.
When the setting dialog is closed with Close, it reports OK if at least one Apply was done during this opening, and Cancel otherwise.
The 'supported on' box shows the supported platform name, or is empty when the policy declares none.
The help box shows the policy's explanation reformatted for reading.

For a policy that applies to both computer and user, the section dropdown is available and starts on Computer unless User was requested. For a policy of one section only, the dropdown is disabled and fixed to that section.
Option controls are built only when the policy declares elements and has a presentation; otherwise the dialog offers only Not configured, Enabled and Disabled.
A number option with a spinner is a spin box limited to the policy's minimum and maximum, stepping by the presentation's increment and starting at its default.
A number option without a spinner is a plain text box, starting at the presentation's default.

In a plain number box, text that is not a whole number is replaced by the default, a number above the policy's maximum is replaced by the maximum, and one below the minimum is replaced by the minimum.
A plain number box accepts only digits and control keys; any other key press is ignored, so a minus sign cannot be typed.
A text option is a text box starting at the default and limited to the policy's maximum length.
A check box option starts checked or unchecked as the presentation's default says.
A combo box option (editable text with suggestions) starts at its default text, is limited to the policy's maximum length, and lists its suggestions sorted unless the presentation says not to sort.

A dropdown option lists the policy's choices by their display names for the policy's language, sorted unless the presentation says not to sort, and starts on the presentation's default choice when there is one.
A list option opens a list editor on its Edit button, with names entered by the person only when the policy says they provide names; the list is kept only if the editor is confirmed with OK.
A multi-line text option is a text box allowing several lines, without wrapping.
When a policy is Disabled in the chosen section, the Disabled choice is selected; when Enabled, the Enabled choice is selected.

When a policy is Enabled, each option control shows the stored value: numbers in number boxes, text in text or combo boxes, the choice in dropdowns (left unselected if no choice matches), ticks in check boxes, lines in multi-line boxes, and the list kept for list options.
When a policy is neither Enabled nor Disabled in the chosen section, Not configured is selected.
Apply and OK are available only when the chosen section's policy source can be written to; for a read-only source they are disabled.
The comment box is disabled and reads "Comments unavailable for this policy source" when the source has no comments; otherwise it shows the policy's saved comment, or is empty when it has none.
Applying first removes the policy's existing configuration in the chosen section, so a setting changed to Not configured leaves no trace.

Applying with Enabled selected stores the policy as Enabled together with the value of every option control: numbers, text, tick state, the chosen dropdown entry, the list and the lines of multi-line text.
Applying with Disabled selected stores the policy as Disabled; with Not configured selected nothing is stored.
The comment is changed only when the policy source supports comments; otherwise it is left alone.
Applying with an empty comment box removes the policy's existing comment, so the policy no longer has a comment.
Applying with a non-empty comment box saves that text as the policy's comment, adding it or replacing the previous one.
Each time the dialog opens, the record of applied changes is cleared.
The option controls are enabled only when Enabled is selected; with Not configured or Disabled they are disabled.
Choosing User in the section dropdown makes the user policy source, loader and comments current; any other choice makes the computer ones current.
OK applies the settings and closes the dialog with OK.
Apply applies the settings, keeps the dialog open and records that changes were made.
When the dialog is closed after any Apply, it reports OK.
The export dialog starts with the chosen key path, the root HKEY_CURRENT_USER\ for the user policy file or HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\ for the computer one, and an empty file name.
The file chooser lists only Registry scripts (*.reg), and the chosen file name fills the export file box only when the person confirms.
When Escape is pressed in the dialog, it closes as cancelled and nothing in it is applied.
When Export is pressed with no file name, it is refused with the message "Please specify a filename and path for the exported REG." and the dialog stays open.

When Export is pressed with a file name, the policy file's entries under the chosen key are written to a REG file under the shown root, the person is told "REG exported successfully.", and the dialog closes with OK.
When writing the REG file fails for any reason, the person is told "Failed to export REG!" and the dialog stays open.
